source.title: On an unsolved problem from the theory of Boolean algebras

accepted.question_text: Let A be a set and let S(A) denote the Boolean algebra of all subsets of A. A principal ideal of S(A) is the ideal consisting of all subsets of one fixed subset X of A. Suppose A has cardinality less than the first aleph inaccessible in the weak sense, with the parallel strict-sense variant stated in the source. Is every sigma-ideal I of S(A) for which the quotient Boolean algebra S(A)/I is complete necessarily principal?

evidence.quote: Are principal ideals the only o-ideals I of S(2) such that S(9)/I is complete? 10).

trace.notes: Original zbMATH URL was blocked by a Cloudflare challenge in the browser-facing web page, so the zbMATH REST API was used only as resolver metadata. The API identified Zbl 0040.31204, DOI 10.4064/cm-2-1-27-29, EuDML 209968, title, author, and publication data. EuDML exposed the readable full PDF link http://matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/cm/cm2/cm217.pdf, which was downloaded to the local temp path used as the extraction artifact.

Mapped the PDF/OCR artifact. The source contains the article title and setup on printed page 27, the explicit problem statement on printed page 28, and a following theorem with proof spanning printed pages 28-29. Key terminology includes S(A) as the field of all subsets of an abstract set, principal ideals, sigma-ideals, complete Boolean algebras, and weak/strict inaccessible alephs.

Extracted one explicit problem block asking whether principal ideals are the only sigma-ideals I of S(A) making S(A)/I complete, under a cardinality bound below the first inaccessible aleph. No solved label or explicit resolution of this problem was present in the source.

Rewrote the OCR problem into a standalone Boolean-algebra question by inlining the source-supported meanings of S(A), principal ideal, quotient Boolean algebra, completeness, and the cardinality bound. The rewritten form avoids source-pointing language.

Accepted. The candidate is explicit, has page-numbered evidence from the resolved PDF/OCR source, is not marked solved, and the rewrite does not add unsupported mathematical claims beyond standard expansion of the notation used in the problem statement.
